# Likelihood / Event-Ordering Test

[← Optiver](../README.md) · [Every Optiver question](../../optiver.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/likelihood-ordering-test)

`data-analysis` `new-round` `probability`

---

## Format

- Approximately 15 questions, with about 90 seconds allotted to each, appeared in the 2026 QR/PhD sessions and replaced some of the traditional mini-games in the PhD stream.
- Every item presents a chart, scatterplot, network visualization, sizable data table, boxplot, or regression fit, together with **three events**, and asks you to rank those events from most likely to least likely.
- The events are usually **not mutually exclusive**, so ordering them precisely can be difficult — the task tests well-calibrated data intuition rather than calculation.
- Pay attention to the submission controls: items are moved with up/down buttons, which are easy to click incorrectly; reserve time to confirm the sequence before the clock runs out.

## Illustrations

Reported prompts (rephrased):

- Scores for students A, B, and C across five exams; rank: (1) A beats B on the following test, (2) C scores at least 90, (3) B and C are separated by over 20 points.
- A scatterplot of x against y with a fitted straight-line regression; rank: (1) the line predicts above the value of a new point at a specified x, (2) a newly observed point has y greater than 20, (3) a third event.
- A 10×10 area containing two random walkers, A and B; rank: (1) A leaves the area before B, (2) B leaves before A, (3) A and B encounter each other within the area.

## Notes

- Determining the exact probability of every choice in 90 seconds is usually unrealistic; the intended strategy is to identify the obviously unlikely event and compare the probabilities of the remaining two.
- Since this part was added recently, its question bank has not been broadly shared — be prepared to depend on basic probability and statistics intuition.

## Preparation

- Train yourself to interpret charts and regressions quickly for directional judgments (over- or under-prediction, tail likelihoods, and correlation magnitude) instead of exact point estimates.
- Check the forum again shortly before the interview, as this section is still changing and additional examples appear each cycle.
